question: A 70-year-old man with 29,000 leukocytes / mm3, 180,000 platelets / mm3 and 15g / dL of hemoglobin in a routine analysis. During the examination no adenopathies or organomegalies were observed. In the extension of the peripheral blood numerous shadows of Gumprecht are detected. What is the most likely diagnosis ?:
analysis: The presence of numerous Gumprecht shadows in the peripheral blood along with the given laboratory values suggests a diagnosis of Chronic lymphoid leukemia (CLL). CLL is a type of leukemia characterized by the accumulation of abnormal lymphocytes in the blood and bone marrow. The typical findings in CLL include lymphocytosis, anemia, and thrombocytopenia. Gumprecht shadows are remnants of disrupted lymphocytes seen in CLL.
